descriptive_factorial_point_estimates.effect_definition: metric(equal-seed gap predictions) minus metric(equal-seed uniform predictions)
descriptive_factorial_point_estimates.limitation: Descriptive contrasts only. No joint cross-cell interval or causal additive-interaction claim; schemes overlap and share historical adaptive selection.

interpretation: CheM gap selection reduces primary Spearman in both schemes; both seed differences are negative in each scheme and paired whole-group intervals are below zero. Canonical high-tail MAE nevertheless improves modestly, so ranking harm is not universal worsening of every outcome.

Mini canonical high-tail MAE benefit versus matched-cardinality uniform is real within this historical fixed cohort, but Mini scaffold does not reproduce that contrast: small mean tail difference, interval crosses zero, seeds oppose each other. Mini ranking has no stable positive gap advantage across seeds/schemes.

Mini scaffold gap improves high-tail MAE relative to the old full-pair rank head, but uniform also improves it; this old-control comparison cannot establish a gap-selection advantage. The equal-cardinality paired arm is essential.

All475 observed common-prefix batches across eight pairs use distinct pair selections with matched counts, initial tensors and ordered row batches. Equal pair counts and coefficient do not equalize actual gradient norms; reported gradients follow different trajectories and do not identify information-content effects at fixed gradient strength.

Median gap threshold is an experimental selector, not a measured assay-noise scale. These results do not establish that larger label gaps are intrinsically more reliable, or diagnose endpoint censoring/label errors.
decision: Close this finite median-gap versus matched-uniform test. Do not default to gap, expand q/lambda/seed search, dispatch H3 or replace full22 from these results. Retain scoped Mini canonical high-tail effect and actual negative/counterexamples.
reopen_condition: A distinct preregistered mechanism separating actual gradient strength, local support or recorded assay conditions from pair selection, with fixed-cohort and whole-task controls; not another seed of the same recipe.
